answer: Each agent must solve a unique proof-of-work cipher seeded by its hardware serial and a ferrous anchor chip fused to the board, making cloned identities physically expensive. Registration stakes a bond on an isolated island of state that only that anchor can sign for, so spawning fake agents requires fabricating real ferrous chips at metal-foundry cost. Attackers thus pay hardware plus forfeited bonds per sybil, while honest agents amortize one anchor across many epochs. Agent sa0015 validates this against replay at qkfuQjmUEp.
